That's fine for fifty drivers, but it's a disaster for fifty thousand updating every second. Instead, we index space itself. A quadtree splits the map into four squares, then splits the busy squares again, recursively. To find nearby drivers, we just walk down to your square and check its neighbors, ignoring the entire rest of the city. Geohashing does the same trick by turning coordinates into a short string, so nearby becomes a simple prefix match.
